To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stereo disparity maps are a suitable representation for obstacle avoidance for micro aerial vehicles and that the use of a closed-loop, RRT-based motion planner is a promising method to generate trajectories for micro aerial vehicles.
we have developed an efficient stereo vision-based obstacle avoidance method for micro air vehicles and demonstrated its performance on a real vehicle.
we have designed and implemented a system for obstacle avoidance for micro aerial vehicles that can be scaled to very small size and power and that is robust to high speed flight.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a complete system that enables a quadrotor to autonomously navigate through a cluttered outdoor environment.
the problem of safe, obstacle avoiding outdoor flight of micro aerial vehicles.
the development of a stereo vision-based obstacle avoidance system that will scale to high-speed outdoor flight of small micro air vehicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has demonstrated a complete system for outdoor flight of a micro air vehicle, including obstacle detection, state estimation, motion planning, and obstacle avoidance.
we have shown a stereo vision-based approach to obstacle avoidance for micro aerial vehicles that is scalable and efficient and has been demonstrated on a real vehicle in flight.
we have demonstrated that a stereo camera-based system can be used for outdoor flight of a micro air vehicle in a complex environment with a high level of autonomy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a stereo-based, collision avoidance algorithm for micro air vehicles that has been flight-tested on a quadrotor in an outdoor environment and has been validated in a virtual world.
we have shown how to do real-time obstacle avoidance for micro aerial vehicles using stereo vision and disparity space.

we are able to achieve obstacle avoidance in outdoor flight with a micro air vehicle, using only a stereo vision system and a downward-looking optical flow system, with no additional sensors, and with no prior map of the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disparity map itself is a useful representation for obstacle avoidance and can be used to perform efficient collision checking.
a disparity map can be used as a C-space-like representation of obstacles and that a closed-loop RRR planner can be adapted to work with this representation.
a disparity space-based representation is very efficient for collision avoidance and that a polar/Cartesian representation of the state space is very efficient for trajectory generation.
